Fixed. crl = [] instead of crl = ["std"], and no_std CRL checking works.

The bead was right and the implication turned out to buy nothing. Audited what std the crl-gated code actually used: crl.rs had four std:: references, three of them `use std::borrow::Cow` and one naming it inline in a return type, plus one vec!. Cow is owned by alloc and merely re-exported by std. signer_discovery.rs had five std:: references, all inside #[cfg(test)] code (std::fs::read, std::slice::from_ref), which is irrelevant to the gate. lib.rs and ocsp.rs had zero.

So the fix was the cfg-gated-import pattern pkix-path already uses, not a refactor.

Evidence: all eight combinations of crl/ocsp/std build under -D warnings, and cargo hack check -p pkix-revocation --feature-powerset --no-dev-deps is clean. Full workspace gate green, 2348 tests.

Two subtleties worth recording, both found by building rather than reasoning:

1. extern crate alloc is gated on all(not(std), crl), not just not(std). The looser gate FAILS the bare --no-default-features build with unused_extern_crates, and that build passes at baseline -- so I would have introduced a regression while fixing this. Caught by testing the whole matrix against the pre-change baseline instead of only the combination I cared about.

2. No #[macro_use] on it, unlike pkix-path. pkix-path wants alloc macros crate-wide; this crate needs vec! in one module and imports it by path. An unused #[macro_use] is itself an error in the combination where crl is off.

One consequence for consumers, documented in the feature comment: enabling crl alone no longer transitively enables std, so it no longer brings std::error::Error on Error. A std consumer who relied on that should name std explicitly alongside crl. Cargo features are additive, so this is the narrow case -- someone enabling ONLY crl in a std build.

Left alone: ocsp still implies std. It has no non-test std usage either, so the same treatment likely applies, but it also pulls dep:x509-ocsp, dep:sha1 and dep:sha2, and that was outside the scope of this bead. Worth its own issue if no_std OCSP is wanted.
